products.name: Eddy Merckx Hour bike
products.text: Round steel tubes, a fixed gear and nothing else. Every later machine in this wing is an argument with this one.

facts.text: Eddy Merckx set the Hour record in Mexico City on 25 October 1972.
The display board beside the bike reads 49.431 km.
Orange lugged steel frame, round tubes, drop bars in white tape, 32-spoke box rims, no brakes.
Frame angles and lengths scaled from the photograph.

ref.title: File:EddyMerckxHourRecordBike.jpg
ref.caption: On display at Eddy Merckx metro station, Brussels

products.name: Graeme Obree's bikes
products.text: Built at home, raced against the world. The tuck came first; the bike was made to hold it.

facts.text: Graeme Obree set the Hour record in Hamar, Norway, on 17 July 1993, on a bike he built himself.
The Riverside Museum display shows white round-tube frames lettered G. OBREE, on tri-spoke wheels.
This model follows the displayed frames, not a specific record machine; narrow bars stand for his tucked position.

ref.title: File:Graeme Obree display at the Riverside Museum.jpg
ref.caption: Riverside Museum, Glasgow

products.name: Lotus Type 108
products.text: No tubes at all: one wing, one blade at each end. It made every frame beside it look like scaffolding.

facts.text: Chris Boardman won the 4,000 m individual pursuit at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992 on this design.
A single carbon wing, a monoblade fork and a single rear stay; rear disc, front tri-spoke, bullhorn bar with extensions.
Wing outline and stay depth scaled from the photograph.

products.name: Zipp 2001
products.text: Take away the seat tube and hang the rider off a beam. The rules later insisted on two triangles; this is why.

facts.text: The reference shows two Zipp 2001 frames, one black and one red: a carbon beam from the head tube over the rear wheel, no seat tube.
Year given as the early 1990s; wheels, bars and drivetrain are a study, not the frames' original build.

products.name: Stevens triathlon bike
products.text: The triathlon superbike as most age-groupers met it: deep tubes, deep wheels, everything pointed forward.

facts.text: Photographed racked at a triathlon: white and red frame with black, deep spoked carbon wheels, aero bars and extensions, a bottle in the frame.
Year not recorded on the photograph; tube depths are a silhouette study.

products.name: Aluminium triathlon bike
products.text: A road frame made fast with bolt-on parts: clip-ons and tri-spokes. How most triathletes went aero in the 2000s.

facts.text: Black aluminium frame with round oversized tubes, clip-on aero bars, tri-spoke wheels with tan-wall tyres (photographed December 2005).
Maker not identified from the photograph; shown as a type of its time.

products.name: Funny bike
products.text: Drop the front of the bike and the rider drops with it. A smaller front wheel was the first aero position you could buy.

facts.text: Low-profile 'funny bikes' with a smaller front wheel were used in time trials and on the track in the 1980s.
No maker is modelled. 24-inch front wheel, 700c rear disc, sloping top tube, bullhorn bar.

products.name: Track pursuit bike
products.text: Four kilometres on a velodrome, alone. Everything that does not push or steer has been taken off.

facts.text: No maker is modelled. Seat tube curved round the rear wheel, fixed gear with a solid chainring, discs front and rear, no brakes.

products.name: Disc-brake triathlon superbike
products.text: The long-course bike carries its own race: food on the top tube, a bottle between the arms, two more behind the saddle.

facts.text: No maker is modelled. Deep truncated-airfoil tubes, dropped stays, integrated nose, storage on the top tube, a bottle between the arms and two behind the saddle, rear disc.

products.name: Road bike with clip-on aero bars
products.text: The cheapest watts ever sold: bolt two tubes to a road bar and fold the rider in half.

facts.text: Clip-on aero bars, first used by triathletes, reached Grand Tour time trials at the end of the 1980s.
No maker is modelled. Steel road frame, drop bars with clip-on extensions, 32-spoke wheels.

products.name: Low-profile triathlon bike, 650c
products.text: Small wheels, steep seat, the rider pitched forward over the bars: the triathlon bike stops pretending to be a road bike.

facts.text: Many 1990s triathlon frames used smaller 650c wheels to bring the rider lower and forward.
No maker is modelled. 650c wheels front and rear, 80° seat angle, aero tubes, rear disc.

products.name: Modern Hour bike
products.text: Everything the pursuit bike learned, stretched over sixty minutes: narrower, lower, and built around the rider's shoulders.

facts.text: No maker is modelled. Truncated-airfoil tubes, seat tube curved round the rear wheel, discs front and rear, narrow extensions, fixed gear, no brakes.

products.name: Draft-legal triathlon bike
products.text: The fastest bike that is still allowed to ride in a bunch: a road bike with its elbows tucked in.

facts.text: In draft-legal triathlon, riders use road bikes; clip-on bars must not reach past the brake levers.
No maker is modelled. Aero road frame, drop bars with short clip-ons, deep spoked wheels.

products.name: Kona concept 2030
products.text: What the long-course bike might become when the rules stop moving: deeper, narrower, everything inside.

facts.text: A studio design, not a product. Deeper kamm sections, very steep seat angle, integrated storage, discs front and rear.

products.name: Small-frame triathlon bike, 650c
products.text: For shorter riders: 650c wheels keep the handling and the position right on a small frame.

facts.text: A studio design. 650c wheels, short reach, low stack, steep seat angle.

products.name: XL triathlon bike
products.text: For tall riders: long stack, long reach, the same aero lines scaled up.

facts.text: A studio design. Stack and reach for a rider around 1.95 m.

products.name: Entry alloy triathlon bike
products.text: The bike most first-timers start on: an alloy frame, clip-ons and good wheels.

facts.text: A studio design. Round alloy tubes, clip-on bars, box-section spoked wheels.

products.name: Track sprint bike
products.text: The opposite of the Hour: short, stiff and built for 200 metres.

facts.text: A studio design. Short wheelbase, drop bars, disc rear and tri-spoke front.

products.name: Beam triathlon concept
products.text: The beam bike returns where the rules allow it: triathlon, not the UCI.

facts.text: A studio design inspired by 1990s beam frames. No seat tube; the saddle rides on a cantilevered beam.

products.name: Wing frame, road triathlon
products.text: The monocoque wing on a road-going triathlon bike: bottles, brakes and all.

facts.text: A studio design using the monocoque wing architecture with a spoked front wheel and aero bars.

products.name: Aero gravel bike
products.text: Drop bars, deep tubes, wider tyres: time-trial ideas on a dirt road.

facts.text: A studio design. Aero road frame with short clip-ons and deep spoked wheels.
